stemBlocks.value: Express x² + 6x + 5 in the form (x + h)² + k by completing the square.
Think first: Halve the coefficient of x — that number goes inside the bracket.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p101-q01 from workbook page 101.

solutionSteps.instruction: Subtract that extra 9 and add the original constant 5.

strategyBlocks.value: Halve the x coefficient to build the squared bracket, subtract the square you introduced, then add the original constant.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x² + 6x + 5 = (x + 3)² − 4. (The same expression also factorises as (x + 1)(x + 5).)

whyThisWorks.value: Expanding (x + h)² always produces x² + 2hx + h², so choosing h as half the x coefficient reproduces the first two terms exactly. The square h² that comes along for free is then subtracted to restore the original constant, giving an expression that is identical to the first but written as a shifted square.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the whole coefficient 6 in the bracket instead of half of it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the whole coefficient 6 in the bracket instead of half of it.
Avoid this: Adding 9 instead of subtracting it.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to bring the original constant 5 down into the final line.

examTip.value: The completed square form hands you the turning point free: (x + 3)² − 4 has its minimum value −4 when x = −3.
